*Maintain a package-based dotfiles checkout and verify its home-directory links.*

> **Change only selected managed configuration; preserve unrelated files, local overrides, credentials and application state.**

## Why install this

Dotfile maintenance can replace a local override or link an entire application
folder into Git. This skill inspects the package allowlist and each destination
before guiding edits and selected-package link changes. It follows a checkout at
`~/localrepo/dotfiles` while accepting any explicit checkout and target home.

## What you get

| Path | What it provides |
|---|---|
| `skills/dotfiles/SKILL.md` | What the agent reads: triggers, the flow, and the one rule. |
| `skills/dotfiles/scripts/` | The deterministic half — `inspect`, `verify`, `report`. |
| `skills/dotfiles/references/layout.md` | Portable packages.json layout, explicit checkout and target resolution, shared versus machine-owned configuration. |
| `skills/dotfiles/references/maintenance.md` | Edit, add-package, setup, preview, link, unlink and conflict recovery procedures with focused checks. |
| `skills/dotfiles/references/baseline.md` | Real-run provenance, privacy-preserving normalization and offline baseline refresh. |
| `skills/dotfiles/skill-invariants.json` | The prose guardrails and the baseline eval declaration. |

## Quick start

Claude Code — run in chat:

```text
/plugin marketplace add natejswenson/claude-skills
/plugin install dotfiles@claude-skills
/dotfiles
```

Codex — run in a terminal from the root of this repository checkout:

```bash
codex plugin marketplace add "$PWD"
codex plugin add dotfiles@claude-skills
```

Start a new Codex session, then invoke in chat:

```text
$dotfiles
```

For direct read-only inspection from this repository checkout:

```bash
node skills/dotfiles/skills/dotfiles/scripts/dotfiles.js inspect --repo "$HOME/localrepo/dotfiles" --target "$HOME"
node skills/dotfiles/skills/dotfiles/scripts/dotfiles.js verify --repo "$HOME/localrepo/dotfiles" --target "$HOME" --package zsh
```

Use your actual package name. In an installed plugin, resolve scripts relative to
its loaded SKILL.md; installation does not put a `dotfiles` binary on PATH.

## Triggers

- "manage my dotfiles"
- "add this config to my dotfiles"
- "check my dotfile links"
- "set up my dotfiles"
- "remove this dotfiles package"
- Anything the method in `SKILL.md` covers, whether or not it is phrased that way.

## Requirements

- **Claude Code:** Local file/shell access and Node 18+. No app connection is needed.
- **Codex:** The same scripts, runtimes and local file/shell access. No app connection is needed; Claude connections are not imported.
- **Personal data:** Configuration stays in the user's selected dotfiles checkout and home. The skill creates no account store. Existing `~/.claude/` and `~/.codex/` machine-owned data remain in place.

GNU Stow is needed for linking, Git for source review, and any repository-specific
runtimes for its own tests. The bundled checker has no npm dependencies.
See [Codex migration notes](../../docs/codex-migration.md).

## Expected layout

`packages.json` lists package directories. Their contents mirror paths below the
target home; `scripts`, `tests` and `specs` are tooling. Use individual file links,
explicit source/target paths and `--no-folding`. Package choices and personal
settings are the user's, not bundled defaults. See the [layout contract](skills/dotfiles/references/layout.md).

## Maintenance and limits

The agent can edit shared sources, add packages, preview/apply selected links,
unlink packages and preserve individual conflicts. The bundled CLI only inspects,
verifies and renders metadata. A successful inspection does not model Stow's
ignore policy or authorize mutation; the agent reviews the real installer and
simulation first. Filename exclusions cannot certify that a configuration is free
of secrets. See [maintenance procedures](skills/dotfiles/references/maintenance.md).

## Development

```bash
cd skills/dotfiles/skills/dotfiles
npm test
```

Node skill. `ci / dotfiles` runs the same tests plus the house lints on
every pull request, and `skillfactory verify --skill dotfiles` reports which rung
of the ladder it has reached.
